use ars_components::date_time::{
    date_field::{self, DateSegmentKind},
    time_field,
};
use ars_core::{Env, Service};
use ars_i18n::{CalendarDate, HourCycle, Time};
use proptest::prelude::*;

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
enum DateFieldAction {
    Send(date_field::Event),
    SetControlledValue(Option<CalendarDate>),
    SetDisabled(bool),
    SetReadonly(bool),
    SetInvalid(bool),
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
enum TimeFieldAction {
    Send(time_field::Event),
    SetControlledValue(Option<Time>),
    SetDisabled(bool),
    SetReadonly(bool),
    SetInvalid(bool),
}

fn date(year: i32, month: u8, day: u8) -> CalendarDate {
    CalendarDate::new_gregorian(year, month, day).expect("generated date should be valid")
}

fn date_field_props() -> date_field::Props {
    date_field::Props::new().id("date-field").label("Date")
}

fn time_field_props() -> time_field::Props {
    time_field::Props::new()
        .id("time-field")
        .label("Time")
        .hour_cycle(Some(HourCycle::H12))
        .granularity(time_field::TimeGranularity::Second)
}

fn arb_date() -> impl Strategy<Value = CalendarDate> {
    (1900i32..=2100, 1u8..=12, 1u8..=28).prop_map(|(year, month, day)| date(year, month, day))
}

fn arb_time() -> impl Strategy<Value = Time> {
    (0u8..=23, 0u8..=59, 0u8..=59)
        .prop_map(|(hour, minute, second)| Time::new(hour, minute, second, 0).unwrap())
}

fn arb_editable_kind() -> impl Strategy<Value = DateSegmentKind> {
    prop_oneof![
        Just(DateSegmentKind::Year),
        Just(DateSegmentKind::Month),
        Just(DateSegmentKind::Day),
    ]
}

fn arb_digit() -> impl Strategy<Value = char> {
    (0u8..=9).prop_map(|digit| char::from(b'0' + digit))
}

fn arb_time_editable_kind() -> impl Strategy<Value = DateSegmentKind> {
    prop_oneof![
        Just(DateSegmentKind::Hour),
        Just(DateSegmentKind::Minute),
        Just(DateSegmentKind::Second),
        Just(DateSegmentKind::DayPeriod),
    ]
}

fn arb_date_field_action() -> impl Strategy<Value = DateFieldAction> {
    prop_oneof![
        arb_editable_kind()
            .prop_map(|kind| DateFieldAction::Send(date_field::Event::FocusSegment(kind))),
        Just(DateFieldAction::Send(date_field::Event::BlurAll)),
        arb_editable_kind()
            .prop_map(|kind| DateFieldAction::Send(date_field::Event::IncrementSegment(kind))),
        arb_editable_kind()
            .prop_map(|kind| DateFieldAction::Send(date_field::Event::DecrementSegment(kind))),
        (arb_editable_kind(), arb_digit()).prop_map(|(kind, ch)| DateFieldAction::Send(
            date_field::Event::TypeIntoSegment(kind, ch)
        )),
        arb_editable_kind()
            .prop_map(|kind| DateFieldAction::Send(date_field::Event::TypeBufferCommit(kind))),
        Just(DateFieldAction::Send(date_field::Event::CompositionStart)),
        (arb_editable_kind(), "[0-9]{0,4}".prop_map(String::from)).prop_map(|(kind, text)| {
            DateFieldAction::Send(date_field::Event::CompositionEnd(kind, text))
        }),
        arb_editable_kind()
            .prop_map(|kind| DateFieldAction::Send(date_field::Event::ClearSegment(kind))),
        Just(DateFieldAction::Send(date_field::Event::ClearAll)),
        prop::option::of(arb_date())
            .prop_map(|value| DateFieldAction::Send(date_field::Event::SetValue(value))),
        prop::option::of(arb_date()).prop_map(DateFieldAction::SetControlledValue),
        any::<bool>().prop_map(DateFieldAction::SetDisabled),
        any::<bool>().prop_map(DateFieldAction::SetReadonly),
        any::<bool>().prop_map(DateFieldAction::SetInvalid),
    ]

1	//! Shared helpers for spec-conformance tests.
2	//!
3	//! Per-component tests call [`assert_anatomy`] with the expected scope and
4	//! the expected `(part, kebab-name)` list. The helper checks every facet
5	//! of the `ComponentPart` contract that the spec's §3 anatomy table
6	//! declares:
7	//!
8	//! 1. `Part::scope()` matches the spec's `data-ars-scope` token.
9	//! 2. `Part::all()` produces exactly the declared parts in the declared
10	//!    order.
11	//! 3. Every declared part round-trips through `Part::name()` with the
12	//!    declared kebab-case token.
13	//! 4. `Part::ROOT` equals the first declared part (workspace convention:
14	//!    every `Part` enum's first variant is `Root`).
15	
16	use ars_core::ComponentPart;
17	
18	/// Asserts that the supplied `Part` enum matches the spec's anatomy
19	/// declaration.
20	///
21	/// `expected_scope` is the `#[scope = "..."]` token the spec puts on the
22	/// `data-ars-scope` attribute. `expected_parts` is the ordered list of
23	/// `(part, kebab-name)` pairs from the spec's §3 anatomy table.
24	pub(crate) fn assert_anatomy<P>(expected_scope: &'static str, expected_parts: &[(P, &'static str)])
25	where
26	    P: ComponentPart + core::fmt::Debug + PartialEq,
27	{
28	    assert_eq!(
29	        P::scope(),
30	        expected_scope,
31	        "Part::scope() must match spec §3 anatomy",
32	    );
33	
34	    let actual = P::all();
35	
36	    let actual_names = actual.iter().map(ComponentPart::name).collect::<Vec<_>>();
37	
38	    let expected_names = expected_parts
39	        .iter()
40	        .map(|(_, name)| *name)
41	        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
42	
43	    assert_eq!(
44	        actual_names, expected_names,
45	        "Part::all() name list must equal spec §3 anatomy column \
46	         (scope = {expected_scope:?})",
47	    );
48	
49	    assert_eq!(
50	        actual.len(),
51	        expected_parts.len(),
52	        "Part::all() length must match the number of spec §3 anatomy rows",
53	    );
54	
55	    for (actual_part, (expected_part, expected_name)) in actual.iter().zip(expected_parts) {
56	        assert_eq!(
57	            actual_part.name(),
58	            *expected_name,
59	            "Part {actual_part:?} must produce kebab-name {expected_name:?}",
60	        );
61	        assert_eq!(
62	            actual_part, expected_part,
63	            "Part::all()[i] must equal the expected part value",
64	        );
65	    }
66	
67	    if let Some((first_expected, _)) = expected_parts.first() {
68	        assert_eq!(
69	            &P::ROOT,
70	            first_expected,
71	            "Workspace convention: Part::ROOT (the first variant) must \
72	             equal the first spec-declared part",
73	        );
74	    }
75	}

//! Adapter-provided component ID derivation helpers.
//!
//! [`ComponentIds`] stores a hydration-safe base ID and derives the structural
//! and keyed part IDs used by connect APIs across the workspace.

use alloc::{format, string::String};
use core::fmt;

/// Derives component part IDs from an adapter-provided base ID.
///
/// The base ID comes from the adapter's hydration-safe ID utility
/// (e.g., `use_id()` in ars-leptos, scope ID in ars-dioxus).
/// All relationship attributes (`aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`,
/// `aria-controls`, `aria-activedescendant`) use IDs derived from
/// this single base to guarantee uniqueness and consistency.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ComponentIds {
    base: String,
}

impl ComponentIds {
    /// Creates from an adapter-provided base ID.
    /// The base ID must be unique and hydration-safe.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn from_id(base_id: &str) -> Self {
        debug_assert!(!base_id.is_empty(), "Component base ID must not be empty");

        Self {
            base: String::from(base_id),
        }
    }

    /// Returns the base ID (for the root element).
    #[must_use]
    pub fn id(&self) -> &str {
        &self.base
    }

    /// Derives a part ID: `"{base}-{part}"`.
    ///
    /// Use for fixed structural parts of a component (trigger, content, label, etc.).
    ///
    /// # Examples
    ///
    /// ```
    /// # use ars_core::ComponentIds;
    /// let ids = ComponentIds::from_id("dialog-3");
    /// assert_eq!(ids.part("title"), "dialog-3-title");
    /// assert_eq!(ids.part("content"), "dialog-3-content");
    /// ```
    #[must_use]
    pub fn part(&self, part: &str) -> String {
        format!("{}-{}", self.base, part)
    }

    /// Derives a keyed item ID: `"{base}-{part}-{key}"`.
    ///
    /// Use for per-item IDs in collection components (lists, grids, trees, menus).
    ///
    /// # Examples
    ///
    /// ```
    /// # use ars_core::ComponentIds;
    /// let ids = ComponentIds::from_id("listbox-2");
    /// assert_eq!(ids.item("item", &"option-a"), "listbox-2-item-option-a");
    /// ```
    #[must_use]
    pub fn item(&self, part: &str, key: &impl fmt::Display) -> String {
        format!("{}-{}-{}", self.base, part, key)
    }

    /// Derives a keyed item sub-part ID: `"{base}-{part}-{key}-{sub}"`.
    ///
    /// Use for sub-elements within a keyed item (text label, indicator, etc.).
    ///
    /// # Examples
    ///
    /// ```
    /// # use ars_core::ComponentIds;
    /// let ids = ComponentIds::from_id("listbox-2");
```

584	    /// Returns default CLDR-like week preferences for the locale when a runtime provider
585	    /// is unavailable.
586	    #[must_use]
587	    pub fn for_locale(locale: &Locale) -> Self {
588	        let (default_first_day, weekend_start, weekend_end) = match locale.region() {
589	            Some("US" | "CA" | "AU" | "NZ" | "PH" | "BR" | "JP" | "TH") => {
590	                (Weekday::Sunday, Weekday::Saturday, Weekday::Sunday)
591	            }
592	
593	            Some("IL") => (Weekday::Sunday, Weekday::Friday, Weekday::Saturday),
594	
595	            Some(
596	                "AE" | "BH" | "DZ" | "EG" | "IQ" | "JO" | "KW" | "LY" | "OM" | "QA" | "SA" | "SD"
597	                | "SY" | "YE",
598	            ) => (Weekday::Saturday, Weekday::Friday, Weekday::Saturday),
599	
600	            _ => (Weekday::Monday, Weekday::Saturday, Weekday::Sunday),
601	        };
602	
603	        // Mirrors CLDR supplemental/weekData minDays territory data:
604	        // unlisted regions inherit the `001` default of 1, while this explicit set uses 4.
605	        let minimal_days_in_first_week = match locale.region() {
606	            Some(
607	                "AD" | "AN" | "AT" | "AX" | "BE" | "BG" | "CH" | "CZ" | "DE" | "DK" | "EE" | "ES"
608	                | "FI" | "FJ" | "FO" | "FR" | "GB" | "GF" | "GG" | "GI" | "GP" | "GR" | "HU" | "IE"
609	                | "IM" | "IS" | "IT" | "JE" | "LI" | "LT" | "LU" | "MC" | "MQ" | "NL" | "NO" | "PL"
610	                | "PT" | "RE" | "RU" | "SE" | "SJ" | "SK" | "SM" | "VA",
611	            ) => 4,
612	            _ => 1,
613	        };
614	
615	        let first_day = locale
616	            .first_day_of_week_extension()
617	            .unwrap_or(default_first_day);
618	
619	        Self {
620	            first_day,
621	            weekend_start,
622	            weekend_end,
623	            minimal_days_in_first_week,
624	        }
625	    }

  "content": "//! Grid math for the `Calendar` component.\n//!\n//! Pure functions over a small slice of the parent [`Context`] state: the\n//! visible month/year, the configured first-day-of-week, and the visible\n//! month count. The machine in [`super`] holds the full context and forwards\n//! the relevant fields here so this module stays free of the wider machine\n//! plumbing — useful both for unit testing the math in isolation and for\n//! keeping the §1.6 spec algorithm legible alongside the rest of the\n//! transitions.\n\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\nuse ars_i18n::{CalendarDate, Weekday};\n\n/// Sunday-zero index for a weekday.\n///\n/// The spec's §1.6 grid algorithm uses modulo arithmetic that anchors at\n/// Sunday=0, but [`Weekday`] is iso-numbered (Monday=1..Sunday=7). The local\n/// helper isolates that conversion so every grid call site uses the same\n/// convention.\n#[must_use]\npub(super) const fn weekday_sunday_zero(weekday: Weekday) -> u8 {\n    match weekday {\n        Weekday::Sunday => 0,\n        Weekday::Monday => 1,\n        Weekday::Tuesday => 2,\n        Weekday::Wednesday => 3,\n        Weekday::Thursday => 4,\n        Weekday::Friday => 5,\n        Weekday::Saturday => 6,\n    }\n}\n\n/// Returns `(month, year)` for the month at `offset` from the first visible\n/// month, normalising the result to the 1..=12 month range with a year\n/// adjustment.\n#[must_use]\npub(super) const fn month_year_at_offset(\n    visible_month: u8,\n    visible_year: i32,\n    offset: usize,\n) -> (u8, i32) {\n    let raw_index = visible_month as i64 - 1 + offset as i64;\n    let normalised_month = raw_index.rem_euclid(12) as u8 + 1;\n    let year_delta = raw_index.div_euclid(12) as i32;\n    (normalised_month, visible_year + year_delta)\n}\n\n/// Advances `(month, year)` by `n` months (signed), normalising the month\n/// back into the 1..=12 range.\n#[must_use]\npub(super) const fn advance_month(visible_month: u8, visible_year: i32, n: i32) -> (u8, i32) {\n    let raw_index = visible_month as i64 - 1 + n as i64;\n    let normalised_month = raw_index.rem_euclid(12) as u8 + 1;\n    let year_delta = raw_index.div_euclid(12) as i32;\n    (normalised_month, visible_year + year_delta)\n}\n\n/// Builds the 6-week grid for the month at the supplied offset.\n///\n/// Always returns exactly 6 rows of 7 dates each (42 cells), padded with\n/// leading days from the previous month and trailing days from the next.\n/// The leading-day count is derived from the difference between the first\n/// day of the target month and the configured `first_day_of_week`, modulo 7.\n///\n/// Date arithmetic at the start/end of the supported calendar range\n/// (`new_gregorian` reject) is treated as a no-op: the returned vector is\n/// empty in that case, signalling that the adapter should render an empty\n/// grid for the boundary month rather than panic.\n#[must_use]\npub(super) fn weeks_for(\n    visible_month: u8,\n    visible_year: i32,\n    first_day_of_week: Weekday,\n    offset: usize,\n) -> Vec<[CalendarDate; 7]> {\n    let (target_month, target_year) = month_year_at_offset(visible_month, visible_year, offset);\n\n    let Ok(first_of_month) = CalendarDate::new_gregorian(target_year, target_month, 1) else {\n        return Vec::new();\n    };\n\n    let first_weekday_index = weekday_sunday_zero(first_of_month.weekday());\n    let start_index = weekday_sunday_zero(first_day_of_week);\n    let leading = i32::from((first_weekday_index + 7 - start_index) % 7);\n\n    let Ok(grid_start) = first_of_month.add_days(-leading) else {\n        return Vec::new();\n    };\n\n    let mut weeks: Vec<[CalendarDate; 7]> = Vec::with_capacity(6);\n    let mut current = grid_start;\n    for _ in 0..6 {\n        let row = match build_week(&current) {\n            Some(row) => row,\n            None => return weeks,\n        };\n        weeks.push(row);\n        let Ok(next_week_start) = current.add_days(7) else {\n            return weeks;\n        };\n        current = next_week_start;\n    }\n\n    weeks\n}\n\nfn build_week(start: &CalendarDate) -> Option<[CalendarDate; 7]> {\n    let day0 = start.clone();\n    let day1 = start.add_days(1).ok()?;\n    let day2 = start.add_days(2).ok()?;\n    let day3 = start.add_days(3).ok()?;\n    let day4 = start.add_days(4).ok()?;\n    let day5 = start.add_days(5).ok()?;\n    let day6 = start.add_days(6).ok()?;\n    Some([day0, day1, day2, day3, day4, day5, day6])\n}\n\n/// Whether `date` belongs to a different `(month, year)` than the month at\n/// the given visible-month offset.\n#[must_use]\npub(super) fn is_outside_month_at_offset(\n    date: &CalendarDate,\n    visible_month: u8,\n    visible_year: i32,\n    offset: usize,\n) -> bool {\n    let (target_month, target_year) = month_year_at_offset(visible_month, visible_year, offset);\n    date.month() != target_month || date.year() month_year_at_offset(visible_month, visible_year, offset);\n        date.month() == month && date.year() == year\n    })\n}\n\n/// Ordered weekday sequence starting at `first_day_of_week`, returned as\n/// `(weekday, sunday_zero_index)` pairs so callers can fetch labels from the\n/// `IntlBackend` without re-deriving the index.\n#[must_use]\npub(super) fn ordered_weekdays(first_day_of_week: Weekday) -> [Weekday; 7] {\n    let start = weekday_sunday_zero(first_day_of_week);\n    let mut out = [Weekday::Sunday; 7];\n    for (i, slot) in out.iter_mut().enumerate() {\n        *slot = sunday_zero_to_weekday((start + i as u8) % 7);\n    }\n    out\n}\n\nconst fn sunday_zero_to_weekday(index: u8) -> Weekday {\n    match index % 7 {\n        0 => Weekday::Sunday,\n        1 => }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn month_year_offset_within_same_year() {\n        assert_eq!(month_year_at_offset(1, 2024, 0), (1, 2024));\n        assert_eq!(month_year_at_offset(1, 2024, 2), (3, 2024));\n        assert_eq!(month_year_at_offset(10, 2024, 1), (11, 2024));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn month_year_offset_wraps_into_next_year() {\n        assert_eq!(month_year_at_offset(11, 2024, 2), (1, 2025));\n        assert_eq!(month_year_at_offset(12, 2024, 1), (1, 2025));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn advance_month_handles_negative_into_prev_year() {\n        assert_eq!(advance_month(1, 2024, -1), (12, 2023));\n        assert_eq!(advance_month(3, 2024, -12), (3, 2023));\n        assert_eq!(advance_month(6, 2024, 12), (6, 2025));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn weeks_for_january_2024_sunday_start_has_leading_days_from_december() {\n        let weeks = weeks_for(1, 2024, Weekday::Sunday, 0);\n        assert_eq!(weeks.len(), 6);\n        // January 1, 2024 is a Monday, so with Sunday-start the first row\n        // starts on December 31, 2023.\n        let first = &weeks[0][0];\n        assert_eq!(first.year(), 2023);\n        assert_eq!(first.month(), 12);\n        assert_eq!(first.day(), 31);\n        // Second cell is January 1, 2024.\n        let second = &weeks[0][1];\n        assert_eq!(second.year(), 2024);\n        assert_eq!(second.month(), 1);\n        assert_eq!(second.day(), 1);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn weeks_for_january_2024_monday_start_first_cell_is_january_first() {\n        let weeks = weeks_for(1, 2024, Weekday::Monday, 0);\n        assert_eq!(weeks.len(), 6);\n        let first = &weeks[0][0];\n        assert_eq!(first.year(), 2024);\n        assert_eq!(first.month(), 1);\n        assert_eq!(first.day(), 1);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn ordered_weekdays_starts_at_configured_day() {\n        assert_eq!(\n            ordered_weekdays(Weekday::Sunday),\n            [\n                Weekday::Sunday,\n                Weekday::Monday,\n                Weekday::Tuesday,\n                Weekday::Wednesday,\n                Weekday::Thursday,\n                Weekday::Friday,\n                Weekday::Saturday,\n            ],\n        );\n        assert_eq!(\n            ordered_weekdays(Weekday::Monday),\n            [\n                Weekday::Monday,\n                Weekday::Tuesday,\n                Weekday::Wednesday,\n                Weekday::Thursday,\n                Weekday::Friday,\n                Weekday::Saturday,\n                Weekday::Sunday,\n            ],\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn is_outside_month_detects_leading_and_trailing_days() {\n        let weeks = weeks_for(1, 2024, Weekday::Sunday, 0);\n        // First date is December 31, 2023, which is outside January 2024.\n        assert!(is_outside_month_at_offset(&weeks[0][0], 1, 2024, 0));\n        // January 1 is inside.\n        assert!(!is_outside_month_at_offset(&weeks[0][1], 1, 2024, 0));\n        // Last row generally contains February dates.\n        assert!(is_outside_month_at_offset(&weeks[5][6], 1, 2024, 0));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn is_in_visible_range_with_multiple_months() {\n        let jan = CalendarDate::new_gregorian(2024, 1, 15).unwrap();\n        let feb = CalendarDate::new_gregorian(2024, 2, 15).unwrap();\n        let mar = CalendarDate::new_gregorian(2024, 3, 15).unwrap();\n        assert!(is_in_visible_range(&jan, 1, 2024, 2));\n        assert!(is_in_visible_range(&feb, 1, 2024, 2));\n        assert!(!is_in_visible_range(&mar, 1, 2024, 2));\n        assert!(is_in_visible_range(&mar, 1, 2024, 3));\n    }\n}\n"

under the active selection mode.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn is_selected(&self, date: &CalendarDate) -> bool {\n        match self.selection_mode {\n            SelectionMode::Single => self.is_selected_single(date),\n            SelectionMode::Multiple => self.is_selected_multi(date),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Whether `date` is disabled (out of min/max or globally disabled).\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn is_date_disabled(&self, date: &CalendarDate) -> bool {\n        if self.disabled {\n            return true;\n        }\n        if let Some(min) = &self.min\n            && date < min\n        {\n            return true;\n        }\n        if let Some(max) = &self.max\n            && date > max\n        {\n            return true;\n        }\n        false\n    }\n\n    /// Whether the user's predicate marks `date` as unavailable.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn is_date_unavailable(&self, date: &CalendarDate) -> bool {\n        self.is_date_unavailable_fn\n            .is_some_and(|predicate| predicate(date))\n    }\n\n    /// Clamps `date` into the configured `[min, max]` range.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn clamp_date(&self, date: CalendarDate) -> CalendarDate {\n         && &clamped > max\n        {\n            clamped = max.clone();\n        }\n        clamped\n    }\n\n    /// If the focused date has moved outside the visible month range,\n    /// scrolls the visible months so the focused date is visible. No-op\n    /// when the focused date already lies within the visible range.\n    pub fn sync_visible_to_focused(&mut self) {\n        if !grid_is_in_visible_range(\n            &self.focused_date,\n            self.visible_month,\n            self.visible_year,\n            self.visible_months,\n        ) {\n            self.visible_month = self.focused_date.month();\n            self.visible_year = self.focused_date.year();\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Returns `(month, year)` for the visible month at `offset` from the\n    /// first visible month.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn month_year_at_offset(&self, offset: usize) -> (u8, i32) {\n        grid_month_year_at_offset(self.visible_month, self.visible_year, offset)\n    }\n\n    /// Whether `date` belongs to a month other than the month at the\n    /// given visible-month offset.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn is_outside_month_at_offset(&self, date: &CalendarDate, offset: usize) -> bool {\n        grid_is_outside_month_at_offset(date, self.visible_month, self.visible_year, offset)\n    }\n\n    /// Whether `date`'s month/year matches the first visible month.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn is_outside_visible_month(&self, date: &CalendarDate) -> bool {\n        date.month() != self.visible_month || date.year() != self.visible_year\n    }\n\n    /// Whether `date` falls within any of the visible months.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn is_in_visible_range(&self, date: &CalendarDate) -> bool {\n        grid_is_in_visible_range(\n            date,\n            self.visible_month,\n            self.visible_year,\n            self.visible_months,\n        )\n    }\n\n    /// Builds the 6-week grid for the first visible month.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn weeks(&self) -> Vec<[CalendarDate; 7]> {\n        self.weeks_for(0)\n    }\n\n    /// Builds the 6-week grid for the month at the supplied offset.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn weeks_for(&self, offset: usize) -> Vec<[CalendarDate; 7]> {\n        grid_weeks_for(\n            self.visible_month,\n            self.visible_year,\n            self.first_day_of_week,\n            offset,\n        )\n    }\n\n    /// Returns the ordered weekday list starting at `first_day_of_week`.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn ordered_weekdays(&self) -> [Weekday; weekday labels.\n    HeadRow,\n\n    /// Individual weekday header cell.\n    HeadCell {\n        /// The weekday this cell describes.\n        #[part(default = Weekday::Monday)]\n        day: component.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct Machine;\n\nimpl ars_core::Machine for Machine {\n    type State = State;\n    type Event = Event;\n    type Context = Context;\n    type Props = Props;\n    type Messages = Messages;\n    type Effect = Effect;\n    type Api<'a> = Api<'a>;\n\n    fn init(\n        props: &Self::Props,\n        env: &Env,\n        messages: &Self::Messages,\n    ) -> (Self::State, Self::Context) {\n        let value = match &props.value {\n            Some(controlled) => Bindable::controlled(controlled.clone()),\n            None => Bindable::uncontrolled(props.default_value.clone()),\n        };\n\n        let selected_dates = match &props.selected_dates {\n            Some(set) => Bindable::controlled(set.clone()),\n            None => Bindable::uncontrolled(props.default_selected_dates.clone()),\n        };\n\n        let initial_date = match props.selection_mode {\n            SelectionMode::Single => value.get().clone().unwrap_or_else(|| props.today.clone()),\n            SelectionMode::Multiple => selected_dates\n                .get()\n                .iter()\n                .next()\n                .cloned()\n                .unwrap_or_else(|| props.today.clone()),\n        };\n\n        let locale = env.locale.clone();\n        let first_day_of_week = props\n            .first_day_of_week\n            .unwrap_or_else(|| locale.first_day_of_week(&*env.intl_backend));\n\n        let visible_months = props.visible_months.max(1);\n        let ids = ComponentIds::from_id(&props.id);\n        let focused_date = initial_date;\n        let visible_month = focused_date.month();\n        let visible_year = focused_date.year();\n\n        let ctx = Context {\n            value,\n            selected_dates,\n            selection_mode: props.selection_mode,\n            max_selected: props.max_selected,\n            focused_date,\n            visible_month,\n            visible_year,\n            visible_months,\n            page_behavior: props.page_behavior,\n            min: props.min.clone(),\n            max: props.max.clone(),\n            first_day_of_week,\n            is_rtl: props.is_rtl,\n            disabled: props.disabled,\n            readonly: props.readonly,\n            show_week_numbers: props.show_week_numbers,\n            today: props.today.clone(),\n            is_date_unavailable_fn: props.is_date_unavailable,\n            locale,\n            messages: messages.clone(),\n            intl_backend: Arc::clone(&env.intl_backend),\n            ids,\n        };\n\n        (State::Idle, ctx)\n    }\n\n    #[expect(\n        clippy::too_many_lines,\n        reason = \"calendar transition table keeps state/event behavior in one auditable match\"\n    )]\n    fn transition(\n        _state: &Self::State,\n        event: &Self::Event,\n        ctx: &Self::Context,\n        _props: &Self::Props,\n    ) -> Option<TransitionPlan<Self>> {\n        if ctx.disabled {\n            return None;\n        }\n\n        match event {\n            Event::FocusIn => ctx.sync_visible_to_focused();\n                }))\n            }\n\n            Event::SelectDate { date } => match ctx.selection_mode {\n                SelectionMode::Single => apply_select_single(ctx, date.clone()),\n                SelectionMode::Multiple => apply_toggle_multi(ctx, date.clone()),\n            },\n\n            Event::ToggleDate { date } => match ctx.selection_mode {\n                SelectionMode::Single => apply_select_single(ctx, date.clone()),\n                SelectionMode::Multiple => apply_toggle_multi(ctx, date.clone()),\n            },\n\n            Event::NextMonth => Some(month_step_plan(step_for_page_behavior(ctx))),\n            Event::PrevMonth => Some(month_step_plan(-step_for_page_behavior(ctx))),\n            Event::NextYear => Some(month_step_plan(12)),\n            Event::PrevYear => Some(month_step_plan(-12)),\n\n            Event::SetMonth { month } => {\n                let month = *month;\n {\n                let year = *year;\n                Some(\n                    TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx: &mut Context| {\n                        ctx.visible_year = year;\n     Api::new(state, context, props, send)\n    }\n}\n\nfn step_for_page_behavior(ctx: &Context) -> i32 {\n    match ctx.page_behavior {\n        PageBehavior::Visible => Some(TransitionPlan::to(State::Focused).apply(move |ctx: &mut Context| {\n        ctx.value.set(Some(date.clone()));\n        ctx.focused_date = date;\n    }))\n}\n\nfn apply_toggle_multi(\n    ctx: &Context,\n    date: CalendarDate,\n) -> Option<TransitionPlan<Machine>> {\n    if ctx.readonly {\n        return None;\n    }\n    if ctx.is_date_disabled(&date) || ctx.is_date_unavailable(&date) {\n        return None;\n    }\n\n    let already_selected = ctx.selected_dates.get().contains(&date);\n    let max_selected = ctx.max_selected;\n    let at_cap = !already_selected\n        && max_selected.is_some_and(|cap| ctx.selected_dates.get().len() >= cap);\n    if at_cap {\n        // Excess toggles are silently dropped per spec §5.4.\n        return None;\n    }\n\n KeyboardKey::PageDown => return Some(month_step_plan(12)),\n            _ => {}\n        }\n    }\n\n    let focused = ctx.focused_date.clone();\n    let (prev_day_key, next_day_key) = if ctx.is_rtl     focused.add_days(-offset).ok()\n            }\n            KeyboardKey::End => {\n                let wd = grid::weekday_sunday_zero(focused.weekday());\n                let start = KeyboardKey::PageUp => focused\n                .add(ars_i18n::DateDuration {\n                    months: -1,\n                    ..ars_i18n::DateDuration::default()\n                })\n                .ok(),\n            KeyboardKey::PageDown => focused\n                .add(ars_i18n::DateDuration {\n                    months: 1,\n                    ..ars_i18n::DateDuration::default()\n {}).then(select_event))\n        }\n        _ => None,\n    }\n}\n\n// ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Api\n// Multi-month\n    /// configurations render the full range via [`Api::range_heading_text`];\n    /// this method always describes the first visible month only.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn    fn grid_attrs_with_ids(&self, grid_id: String, heading_id: String) -> AttrMap {\n        let mut attrs = AttrMap::new();\n        let [(scope_attr, scope_val), (part_attr, part_val)] = usable without any extra trait impls on\n/// the foreign type.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct SelectedDates {\n    dates: Vec<CalendarDate>,\n}\n\nimpl SelectedDates {\n set.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn contains(&self, date: &CalendarDate) -> bool {\n        self.dates\n            .binary_search_by(|candidate| candidate.compare(date))\n            .is_ok()\n    }\n\n    /// Inserts `date` into the set, returning `true` if it was newly added.\n    pub fn insert(&mut self, date: CalendarDate) -> bool {\n        match self.dates.binary_search_by(|candidate| candidate.compare(&date)) {\n            Ok(_) => false,\n            Err(idx) => {\n                self.dates.insert(idx, date);\n                true\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Removes `date` from the set, returning `true` if it was present.\n    pub fn remove(&mut self, date: &CalendarDate) -> bool {\n        match self.dates.binary_search_by(|candidate| candidate.compare(date)) {\n            Ok(idx) => {\n                self.dates.remove(idx);\n                true\n            }\n            Err(_) => false,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Returns the underlying sorted slice.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn as_slice(&self) -> &[CalendarDate] {\n        &self.dates\n    }\n}\n\nimpl FromIterator<CalendarDate> for SelectedDates {\n    fn from_iter<I: IntoIterator<Item = CalendarDate>>(iter: I) -> Self {\n        let mut set = Self::new();\n        for date in iter {\n            set.insert(date);\n        }\n        set\n    }\n}\n\nimpl<'a> IntoIterator for &'a SelectedDates {\n    type Item = &'a CalendarDate;\n    type IntoIter = core::slice::Iter<'a, CalendarDate>;\n    fn into_iter(self) -> Self::IntoIter {\n        self.dates.iter()\n    }\n}\n\n/// Predicate type for marking dates unavailable."
}

---
name: post-implementation-audit
description: MANDATORY after every implementation task — runs three sequential audits on the new code (spec/impl drift, iterative "anything missing?", test coverage) and lands every finding in the same PR before the user-review step. Invoke as soon as an implementation task's named tests pass, OR when any of these phrases appears: "ready to present", "implementation is complete", "named tests pass", "before opening the PR", "ready for review". Skipping this audit leaves spec drift, untested defensive code, missing conventions, and silent contract violations in the merged PR.
---

# Post-implementation audit

This skill is the bridge between *"the named tests pass"* and *"the user reviews the diff"*. It exists because the initial implementation of any task is usually correct on its surface acceptance criteria but quietly drifts from the spec, leaves untested defensive code, ships APIs that diverge from convention, or carries a fold-vs-lowercase mistake that won't surface until production. Running these audits before user-review collapses three reviewer round-trips into one.

The skill is mandatory per CLAUDE.md "Development Workflow" step 7 — run it after implementing any user-requested task (feature, bug fix, refactor) and before presenting the final result for user review.

## Quick flow

The audit is strictly linear — no branching, just a loop in Phase 2:

```
Phase 1 (spec/impl drift audit)
   └─→ land all Phase 1 findings
        └─→ Phase 2 (iterative "anything missing?")
              ├─→ Round 1: surface findings → land all
              ├─→ Round 2: surface findings → land all
              └─→ keep looping until 2 consecutive clean rounds (minimum 2 rounds total)
                   └─→ Phase 3 (test coverage)
                        └─→ land all Phase 3 findings
                             └─→ Final verification suite
                                  └─→ Hand off to user (CLAUDE.md step 8)
```

The body below walks through each phase in order. Read top-to-bottom; the structure mirrors the execution order.

## Operating principle: no deferral

**Every recommendation each audit phase produces lands in *this* PR.** Don't open follow-up issues. Don't TODO-flag. Don't promise a future PR or a future sprint. Don't quietly skip a finding because it feels like scope creep.

If a finding is genuinely out of scope (e.g., requires a workspace-wide refactor touching 50+ files), surface it explicitly to the user with that reasoning visible — but the default is to land everything. This constraint is what makes the audit valuable: a deferred finding is a guarantee that the original implementation's bias survives into `main`, where it costs ten times as much to undo.

The user will tell you "land it all". Anticipate that, and just do it.

## Three sequential phases

Run the phases **in order**. Each phase fully completes (audit → land all findings → re-verify) before the next begins.

---

### Phase 1 — spec/implementation drift audit

Compare the implementation against the authoritative spec (`spec/components/<category>/<component>.md` plus any foundation specs it transitively depends on) section-by-section. For every drift, propose the **best outcome independent of which side is currently right**. Sometimes the spec wins, sometimes the impl wins, sometimes the right answer is neither.

The canonical entry-prompt for this phase (use this wording when the user asks you to start the audit explicitly):

> "Now let's do an audit on how well our new code follows our spec. Do an in-depth check for spec drift and suggest recommendations for each finding. In those recommendations, disregard both the spec and the current implementation as defaults — the recommendation should be the best outcome possible. Sometimes that's the spec, sometimes the implementation, sometimes a mix, sometimes a totally different thing."

#### Precondition: both files must exist

Before reading anything, verify the touched implementation has a corresponding spec file at `spec/components/<category>/<name>.md` (or the relevant `spec/foundation/` path for foundation-layer changes). If the spec is missing, **stop the audit and surface this to the user** — an unspecced module is a planning failure that should be resolved (write the spec, or split the change) before auditing, not papered over by this skill. Likewise, if the implementation file referenced by the issue is missing or empty, surface that as a precondition failure rather than auditing against an empty diff.

#### Procedure

1. Read the spec file end-to-end (use `Read` with no offset/limit so you have the whole thing).
2. Read the implementation file end-to-end (same).
3. Walk every public surface declared in the spec — every struct, enum, function, method, derive list, default value, constant, public re-export. For each:
   - Does the spec define it? Does the impl match exactly?
   - Are there extras in the impl not in the spec? Are they justified?
   - Are there spec items the impl skipped? Are they critical?
   - **Does the spec's prose match the impl's actual behavior?** This is the silent-contract-violation class — words that mean something specific in the spec but were implemented as something close-but-different (e.g., "case folding" in the spec but `to_lowercase` in the impl).
4. For each finding, write up:
   - What the spec says, with line numbers
   - What the impl does, with line numbers
   - Why it drifted (often a tradeoff the implementer made under acceptance-criteria pressure)
   - **Best-outcome recommendation** — independent of which side is currently right
5. Group findings by severity (High / Medium / Low) and present as a table to the user.
6. Land all of them. Update the spec where the impl is right, update the impl where the spec is right, do both where neither was right, change *only* the spec wording (and add tests proving the new wording) when the contract was subtly wrong all along.

#### Special case: both the spec and the implementation are wrong

A small fraction of drift findings are *not* "one side is right, the other drifted" — both sides are incorrect, incomplete, or built on a flawed premise. This is rare but real (the task #204 eszett case is an example: the spec implied `ß ↔ ss` equivalence, the impl used `to_lowercase`, but neither matched the actual TR21 case-folding semantics needed). Handle this case differently from routine drift:

1. **Escalate to the user via `AskUserQuestion`** — don't unilaterally pick a "best outcome" when no precedent exists. A both-wrong case is a real design decision, not a routine drift fix; the user owns the call.
2. **Once the user picks a direction**, land *all three* together in this same PR: the new spec wording, the new implementation, and the tests proving the new design. Skipping any of the three leaves a different kind of drift behind.
3. **Write the test first** (TDD per CLAUDE.md), watch it fail under the old code, then change the impl, then update the spec to describe what the new tests assert.

#### Output table format

| Finding ID | Severity | What spec says | What impl does | Best outcome | Where to land |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| H1 | High | … | … | … | spec §X / impl `path:line` |

End with a disposition summary: *"N spec-only changes, M impl-only changes, K both, Q status-quo-was-correct."*

---

### Phase 2 — iterative "anything else missing?" passes

Once Phase 1 findings are landed, the next blind spot is the surface Phase 1 didn't look at: adapter specs, feature flags, prelude exports, framework wiring, foundation patterns that deserve promotion, catalog/manifest entries. This phase is **iterative** — keep asking "anything else?" until two consecutive rounds find nothing new.

The canonical entry-prompt (one per round):

> "Any other improvement that we might still be missing?"

#### Surfaces to actively check each round

This is a non-exhaustive checklist. Each round, walk through it explicitly:

- **Adapter specs** at `spec/leptos-components/<category>/<component>.md` and `spec/dioxus-components/<category>/<component>.md` — do they describe the new core surface accurately? Are their canonical implementation sketches up-to-date with the actual `Api` / function signatures? Do they reference the right helper methods (e.g., `Api::root_attrs()`) instead of hardcoded data attribute strings?
- **Adapter feature wiring** in `crates/ars-leptos/Cargo.toml` and `crates/ars-dioxus/Cargo.toml` — does the adapter's `icu4x` / `web-intl` feature need to enable any new `ars-components/<feature>` flag for the new code to be reachable?
- **Adapter `prelude.rs`** — does the new public API need to flow through? (Only if an adapter wrapper exists for the new component; if not, defer to the adapter task.)
- **Workspace `spec/manifest.toml`** and **`foundation/02-component-catalog.md`** — is the new component registered and statused? (For brand-new components only.)
- **Foundation specs** (`spec/foundation/00-*` through `spec/foundation/11-*`) — does the new code expose a missing shared abstraction worth promoting? CLAUDE.md `spec/CLAUDE.md` says: *"If an adapter-specific implementation exposes a missing shared abstraction, promote that abstraction into the appropriate foundation/shared spec."*
- **New crate dependencies** — was the user notified per CLAUDE.md's "Do not add a new dependency crate without explicit user approval first" rule? Did the implementation add `i18n`-style feature flags that warrant a CLAUDE.md note?
- **`.cargo/mutants.toml`** — are any new equivalent mutations documented with justifications? (Phase 3 will validate this; surface it here if a mutation that *should* be equivalent isn't documented yet.)

#### Termination

Stop when:

- Two consecutive rounds surface no new findings, **OR**
- Three rounds have been completed and the remaining findings are honestly out-of-scope (genuine workspace-wide refactors that would derail this PR).

Do **not** stop after one clean round — the second round nearly always surfaces items the first ignored because they felt out-of-scope. With the "no deferral" rule active, they're back in scope.
```

# Calendar — Leptos Adapter

## 1. Purpose and Adapter Scope

This spec maps the core [`Calendar`](../../components/date-time/calendar.md) contract onto a Leptos 0.8.x component. The adapter adds the Leptos-facing signature, multi-month rendering structure, node ownership, semantic repair, live-announcement wiring, and SSR-safe rules that the agnostic spec leaves to the adapter.

## 2. Public Adapter API

```rust,no_check
#[component]
pub fn Calendar(
    #[prop(optional)] id: Option<String>,
    #[prop(optional, into)] value: Signal<Option<CalendarDate>>,
    #[prop(optional)] default_value: Option<CalendarDate>,
    #[prop(optional)] min: Option<CalendarDate>,
    #[prop(optional)] max: Option<CalendarDate>,
    #[prop(optional)] disabled: bool,
    #[prop(optional)] readonly: bool,
    #[prop(optional)] first_day_of_week: Option<Weekday>,
    #[prop(optional)] visible_months: usize,
    #[prop(optional)] page_behavior: calendar::PageBehavior,
    #[prop(optional)] show_week_numbers: bool,
```

    1|       |//! `Calendar` component state machine and connect API.
    2|       |//!
    3|       |//! Framework-agnostic implementation of the grid-based date picker defined
    4|       |//! in `spec/components/date-time/calendar.md`. The machine owns visible
    5|       |//! month/year, focused-date roving tab state, single and multi-date
    6|       |//! selection, locale-aware weekday ordering, min/max constraints, and the
    7|       |//! screen-reader announcement intent emitted when the visible month
    8|       |//! changes.
    9|       |//!
   10|       |//! ## Spec-vs-implementation reconciliation
   11|       |//!
   12|       |//! The spec's §1.7 code examples use illustrative pseudo-Rust that
   13|       |//! pre-dates the current `ars-i18n::CalendarDate` API: it treats months and
   14|       |//! days as `NonZero<u8>`, calls `add_days` / `add_months` as infallible,
   15|       |//! and accesses month/day/year as fields. The real types return
   16|       |//! `Result<_, CalendarError>` and expose month/day/year as `u8` methods.
   17|       |//! The implementation here keeps the spec's semantics intact while using
   18|       |//! the real fallible API; cases where the spec implies an arithmetic
   19|       |//! result cannot fail (grid anchoring, focused-date navigation) propagate
   20|       |//! using `?`-style early returns that leave context unchanged rather than
   21|       |//! panic at calendar-system boundaries.
   22|       |//!
   23|       |//! ## Range-calendar drift in spec §1.8
   24|       |//!
   25|       |//! The spec's §1.8 connect API includes `on_cell_hover(date) ->
   26|       |//! Event::HoverDate { date }` and `on_grid_mouseleave() ->
   27|       |//! Event::HoverEnd`, but neither event appears in §1.2 and neither has a
   28|       |//! transition arm. Those entries belong to the future `RangeCalendar`
   29|       |//! component; this implementation omits them and the matching
```

          Sharding method to use when running with --shards

          Possible values:

### Spec / impl reconciliation (intentional)

Documented in `mod.rs` module docs:
- Spec uses `NonZero<u8>` + infallible `add_days/add_months`; real `ars-i18n` API uses `u8` + `Result<_, CalendarError>`. Impl propagates correctly.
- Spec's `BTreeSet<CalendarDate>` requires `Ord`, which `CalendarDate` doesn't implement. Impl introduces `SelectedDates` newtype using `CalendarDate::compare` to keep a sorted set.
- Spec §1.8 references `Event::HoverDate`/`HoverEnd` not declared in §1.2 — **skipped** as range-calendar drift. Flag in PR body for the range-calendar follow-up to clean up. (Confirmed with you up front.)
- `Event::KeyDown` includes `shift: bool` so `Shift+PageUp`/`Shift+PageDown` resolve in a single transition instead of via a side channel.

§5.5 "Shift+Space range from anchor" and "Ctrl+A select-all" multi-select keyboard extras — these require an undefined "anchor" concept in the spec. Named tests don't require them. **Not implemented**; will need spec refinement (separate follow-up).

> AGENT

Yes — several. I followed the rule "implementation changes that shift the contract belong in the spec same task" while coding, but I held off on the actual spec edits to confirm scope with you first. Here's the list, ordered by contract impact:

**Must update (contract-changing):**

1. **`Event::KeyDown` payload.** Spec `KeyDown { key }`; impl `KeyDown { key, shift: bool }`. Folds Shift+PageUp/PageDown into one transition instead of a side-channel `on_grid_keydown(key, shift)`.
2. **`Event::ToggleDate { date }` struct variant.** Spec uses `ToggleDate(CalendarDate)`; impl uses struct form for consistency with `FocusDate`/`SelectDate`.
3. **`Effect` is a typed enum with `AnnounceMonth`**, not the bare `"announce-month"` string. The setup closure no longer calls `use_platform_effects()` — the named intent is sufficient; the adapter does the announce.
4. **Multi-select Props promoted to §1.4 unified Props** (not "additional" in §5.1). `selection_mode`, `max_selected`, `selected_dates`, `default_selected_dates` always present.
5. **`SelectedDates` newtype replaces `BTreeSet<CalendarDate>`.** `CalendarDate` has no `Ord` impl; sorted `Vec` via `CalendarDate::compare` plays the same role.
6. **§1.8 hover surface removed.** `Event::HoverDate`/`HoverEnd`, `Context.is_range`/`range_start`/`range_end`, `on_cell_hover`/`on_grid_mouseleave` belong to the future RangeCalendar; the §1.8 API methods that referenced them are dropped from this component's spec.
7. **`Context.unavailable_dates: Vec<CalendarDate>` field removed.** Was a pre-computed cache of the predicate; impl evaluates the predicate directly. Same behavior, less state.
8. **`Context.ids: ComponentIds` replaces `heading_id`/`grid_id` string fields.** All part IDs derive from `ids.part("heading")`, `ids.part("grid")`, etc.
9. **`CalendarDate` API form.** Spec calls `new_gregorian(year, NonZero::new(month)..., nzu8(day))` infallibly; the real API is `new_gregorian(year: i32, month: u8, day: u8) -> Result<_, CalendarError>` and `add_days/add_months` return `Result`. Code examples need to use the real signatures (with `.expect("reason")` where overflow is impossible by construction).

**Cosmetic/derives:**

10. `PageBehavior` and `SelectionMode` derive `Copy` (the spec omits it).
11. `Messages` has `LocaleLabelFn` / `PageLabelFn` type aliases (clippy `type_complexity`).
12. `Props` `PartialEq` is hand-written, compares `is_date_unavailable` via `core::ptr::fn_addr_eq` (auto-derive warns on fn-pointer comparison).

Want me to land all of these in `spec/components/date-time/calendar.md` now (same PR), or would you like to review the list first?

129	impl Context {
130	    /// Whether the given date is the currently selected value.
131	    pub fn is_selected(&self, date: &CalendarDate) -> bool {
132	        self.value.get().as_ref() == Some(date)
133	    }
134	
135	    /// Whether a date is disabled (outside min/max or globally disabled).
136	    pub fn is_date_disabled(&self, date: &CalendarDate) -> bool {
137	        if self.disabled { return true; }
138	        if let Some(ref min) = self.min {
139	            if date < min { return true; }
140	        }
141	        if let Some(ref max) = self.max {
142	            if date > max { return true; }
143	        }
144	        false
145	    }
146	
147	    /// Whether a date is marked unavailable by the user-provided predicate.
148	    /// Checks both the static `unavailable_dates` list and the dynamic
149	    /// `is_date_unavailable_fn` callback from Props. Unavailable dates are
150	    /// focusable (for keyboard navigation) but not selectable.
151	    pub fn is_date_unavailable(&self, date: &CalendarDate) -> bool {
152	        if self.unavailable_dates.contains(date) {
153	            return true;
154	        }
155	        if let Some(ref predicate) = self.is_date_unavailable_fn {
156	            return predicate(date);
157	        }
158	        false
159	    }
160	
161	    /// Clamp a date into the min/max range.
162	    pub fn clamp_date(&self, date: CalendarDate) -> CalendarDate {
163	        let date = match &self.min {
164	            Some(min) if date < *min => min.clone(),
165	            _ => date,
166	        };
167	        match &self.max {
168	            Some(max) if date > *max => max.clone(),
169	            _ => date,
170	        }
171	    }
172	
173	    /// Ensure the focused date's month is visible.
174	    /// Only scrolls when the focused date falls outside all visible months.
175	    pub fn sync_visible_to_focused(&mut self) {
176	        if !self.is_in_visible_range(&self.focused_date) {
177	            self.visible_month = self.focused_date.month.get();
178	            self.visible_year = self.focused_date.year;
179	        }
180	    }
181	}

  "new_string": "### 1.3 Context\n\n[`CalendarDate`] implements neither `Ord` nor `PartialOrd` — different\ncalendar systems share the same value type so global ordering is undefined,\nbut it does expose chronological [`CalendarDate::compare`](https://docs.rs/ars-i18n).\nBoth `is_date_disabled` and `clamp_date` compare via `compare(...)` rather\nthan `<`/`>`, and the multi-select set lives in a [`SelectedDates`] newtype\n(§1.4) that keeps a sorted `Vec<CalendarDate>` instead of a `BTreeSet`.\n\n```rust\n/// Context for the Calendar component.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug)]\npub struct Context {\n    /// Selected date (single-select mode).\n    pub value: Bindable<Option<CalendarDate>>,\n    /// Selected date set (multi-select mode).\n    pub selected_dates: Bindable<SelectedDates>,\n    /// Active selection mode.\n    pub selection_mode: SelectionMode,\n    /// Cap on `selected_dates.len()` in multi-select mode.\n    pub max_selected: Option<usize>,\n    /// The date that currently holds keyboard focus within the grid.\n    pub focused_date: CalendarDate,\n    /// The first visible month (1-based).\n    pub visible_month: u8,\n    /// The year of the first visible month.\n    pub visible_year: i32,\n    /// Number of months displayed side-by-side (>= 1).\n    pub visible_months: usize,\n    /// Navigation step size for prev/next.\n    pub page_behavior: PageBehavior,\n    /// Minimum selectable date.\n    pub min: Option<CalendarDate>,\n    /// Maximum selectable date.\n    pub max: Option<CalendarDate>,\n    /// Resolved first day of week (locale default unless overridden by Props).\n    pub first_day_of_week: Weekday,\n    /// Whether the calendar is rendered right-to-left.\n    pub is_rtl: bool,\n    /// Whether the calendar is globally disabled.\n    pub disabled: bool,\n    /// Whether the calendar is read-only (focus OK, selection blocked).\n    pub readonly: bool,\n    /// Whether the head row exposes ISO week numbers.\n    pub show_week_numbers: bool,\n    /// Date passed in as \"today\" by the adapter; used to mark today's cell\n    /// with `data-ars-today`.\n    pub today: CalendarDate,\n    /// User-supplied predicate marking dates unavailable. Unavailable dates\n    /// remain focusable but are not selectable. Evaluated lazily — there is\n    /// no pre-computed static cache.\n    pub is_date_unavailable_fn: Option<fn(&CalendarDate) -> bool>,\n    /// Resolved locale (from `Env`).\n    pub locale: Locale,\n    /// Resolved translatable messages.\n    pub messages: Messages,\n    /// Backend used for locale-dependent labels and digits.\n    pub intl_backend: Arc<dyn IntlBackend>,\n    /// Derived part IDs (`ids.part(\"heading\")`, `ids.part(\"grid\")`, …).\n    pub ids: ComponentIds,\n}\n\nimpl Context {\n    /// Whether `date` is selected under the active selection mode.\n    pub fn is_selected(&self, date: &CalendarDate) -> bool {\n        match self.selection_mode {\n            SelectionMode::Single => self.value.get().as_ref() == Some(date),\n            SelectionMode::Multiple => self.selected_dates.get().contains(date),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Whether a date is disabled (outside min/max or globally disabled).\n    pub fn is_date_disabled(&self, date: &CalendarDate) -> bool {\n        if self.disabled { return true; }\n        if let Some(min) = &self.min\n            && date.compare(min) == Ordering::Less\n        {\n            return true;\n        }\n        if let Some(max) = &self.max\n            && date.compare(max) == Ordering::Greater\n        {\n            return true;\n        }\n        false\n    }\n\n    /// Whether the user predicate marks `date` as unavailable.\n    pub fn is_date_unavailable(&self, date: &CalendarDate) -> bool {\n        self.is_date_unavailable_fn\n            .is_some_and(|predicate| predicate(date))\n    }\n\n    /// Clamp `date` into the configured `[min, max]` range.\n    pub fn clamp_date(&self, date: CalendarDate) -> CalendarDate {\n        let mut clamped = date;\n        if let Some(min) = &self.min\n            && clamped.compare(min) == Ordering::Less\n        {\n            clamped = min.clone();\n        }\n        if let Some(max) = &self.max\n            && clamped.compare(max) == Ordering::Greater\n        {\n            clamped = max.clone();\n        }\n        clamped\n    }\n\n    /// Ensure the focused date's month is visible.\n    /// Only scrolls when the focused date falls outside all visible months.\n    pub fn sync_visible_to_focused(&mut self) {\n        if !self.is_in_visible_range(&self.focused_date) {\n            self.visible_month = self.focused_date.month();\n            self.visible_year = self.focused_date.year();\n        }\n    }\n}\n```"

697	    /// Keyboard navigation within the calendar grid.
698	    /// Follows WAI-ARIA Grid pattern with RTL awareness.
699	    fn handle_keydown(
700	        state: &State,
701	        data: &KeyboardEventData,
702	        ctx: &Context,
703	    ) -> Option<TransitionPlan<Self>> {
704	        // Only handle keys when the grid is focused.
705	        if *state != State::Focused { return None; }
706	
707	        let focused = ctx.focused_date.clone();
708	        // RTL-aware directional keys: in RTL, Left means "next" and Right means "prev".
709	        let (prev_day_key, next_day_key) = if ctx.is_rtl {
710	            (KeyboardKey::ArrowRight, KeyboardKey::ArrowLeft)
711	        } else {
712	            (KeyboardKey::ArrowLeft, KeyboardKey::ArrowRight)
713	        };
714	
715	        let new_focus = match data.key {
716	            k if k == prev_day_key => Some(focused.add_days(-1)),
717	            k if k == next_day_key => Some(focused.add_days(1)),
718	            KeyboardKey::ArrowUp              => Some(focused.add_days(-7)),
719	            KeyboardKey::ArrowDown            => Some(focused.add_days(7)),
720	            KeyboardKey::Home                 => {
721	                // Move to start of current week.
722	                let wd = focused.weekday() as u8;
723	                let start = ctx.first_day_of_week as u8;
724	                let offset = ((wd + 7 - start) % 7) as i32;
725	                Some(focused.add_days(-offset))
726	            }
727	            KeyboardKey::End => {
728	                // Move to end of current week.
729	                let wd = focused.weekday() as u8;
730	                let start = ctx.first_day_of_week as u8;
731	                let offset = ((wd + 7 - start) % 7) as i32;
732	                Some(focused.add_days(6 - offset))
733	            }
734	            KeyboardKey::PageUp  => Some(focused.add_months(-1)),
735	            KeyboardKey::PageDown => Some(focused.add_months(1)),
736	            _ => None,
737	        };
738	
739	        // Shift+PageUp/PageDown for year navigation is handled separately
740	        // because the key enum itself doesn't encode the shift modifier.
741	        // Adapters call `on_grid_keydown(data, shift)` which maps:
742	        //   Shift+PageUp   -> Event::PrevYear
743	        //   Shift+PageDown -> Event::NextYear
744	
745	        match new_focus {

  "new_string": "### 1.7 Full Machine Implementation\n\nThe named-effect intent for month/year navigation is a typed enum, not a\nbare `&'static str`. The setup closure is a no-op marker\n([`PendingEffect::named`]); the adapter resolves the announce intent based\non the typed name and calls into its platform announce path — core code\nnever reaches for a framework hook like `use_platform_effects()`.\n\n```rust\n/// Typed identifier for every named effect intent the `calendar` machine emits.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]\npub enum Effect {\n    /// Announce the newly visible month (or month range) to assistive tech\n    /// via the adapter's platform announcer. Triggered by every\n    /// month/year navigation transition.\n    AnnounceMonth,\n}\n\npub struct Machine;\n\nimpl ars_core::Machine for Machine {\n    type State    = State;\n    type Event    = Event;\n    type Context  = Context;\n    type Props    = Props;\n    type Messages = Messages;\n    type Effect   = Effect;\n    type Api<'a>  = Api<'a>;\n\n    fn init(props: &Self::Props, env: &Env, messages: &Self::Messages) -> (Self::State, Self::Context) {\n        let value = match &props.value {\n            Some(controlled) => Bindable::controlled(controlled.clone()),\n            None             => Bindable::uncontrolled(props.default_value.clone()),\n        };\n        let selected_dates = match &props.selected_dates {\n            Some(set) => Bindable::controlled(set.clone()),\n            None      => Bindable::uncontrolled(props.default_selected_dates.clone()),\n        };\n\n        let initial_date = match props.selection_mode {\n            SelectionMode::Single   => value.get().clone().unwrap_or_else(|| props.today.clone()),\n            SelectionMode::Multiple => selected_dates.get().iter().next().cloned()\n                .unwrap_or_else(|| props.today.clone()),\n        };\n\n        let locale = env.locale.clone();\n        let first_day = props\n            .first_day_of_week\n            .unwrap_or_else(|| locale.first_day_of_week(&*env.intl_backend));\n\n        let ctx = Context {\n            value,\n            selected_dates,\n            selection_mode: props.selection_mode,\n            max_selected: props.max_selected,\n            focused_date: initial_date.clone(),\n            visible_month: initial_date.month(),\n            visible_year: initial_date.year(),\n            visible_months: props.visible_months.max(1),\n            page_behavior: props.page_behavior,\n            min: props.min.clone(),\n            max: props.max.clone(),\n            first_day_of_week: first_day,\n            is_rtl: props.is_rtl,\n            disabled: props.disabled,\n            readonly: props.readonly,\n            show_week_numbers: props.show_week_numbers,\n            today: props.today.clone(),\n            is_date_unavailable_fn: props.is_date_unavailable,\n            locale,\n            messages: messages.clone(),\n            intl_backend: Arc::clone(&env.intl_backend),\n            ids: ComponentIds::from_id(&props.id),\n        };\n\n        (State::Idle, ctx)\n    }\n\n    fn transition(\n        _state: &Self::State,\n        event: &Self::Event,\n        ctx: &Self::Context,\n        _props: &Self::Props,\n    ) -> Option<TransitionPlan<Self>> {\n        if ctx.disabled { return None; }\n\n        match event {\n            // ── Focus management ─────────────────────────────────────────\n            Event::FocusIn  => Some(TransitionPlan::to(State::Focused)),\n            Event::FocusOut => Some(TransitionPlan::to(State::Idle)),\n\n            Event::FocusDate { date } => {\n                let clamped = ctx.clamp_date(date.clone());\n                Some(TransitionPlan::to(State::Focused).apply(move |ctx| {\n                    ctx.focused_date = clamped;\n                    ctx.sync_visible_to_focused();\n                }))\n            }\n\n `apply_select_single`, Multiple\n            // uses `apply_toggle_multi`. Read the spec wording in §1.2 for\n            // why they share an arm.\n            Event::SelectDate { date } | Event::ToggleDate { date } => {\n                match ctx.selection_mode {\n                    SelectionMode::Single   => apply_select_single(ctx, date.clone()),\n                    SelectionMode::Multiple => apply_toggle_multi(ctx, date.clone()),\n                }\n            }\n\n            // ── Month / year navigation ──────────────────────────────────\n            Event::NextMonth => Some(month_step_plan(step_for_page_behavior(ctx))),\n            Event::PrevMonth => Some(month_step_plan(-step_for_page_behavior(ctx))),\n            Event::NextYear  => Some(month_step_plan(12)),\n            Event::PrevYear  => Some(month_step_plan(-12)),\n\n            Event::SetMonth { month } => {\n                let month = *month;\n                if !(1..=12).contains(&month) { return None; }\n                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx| {\n                    ctx.visible_month = month;\n                }).with_effect(announce_month_effect()))\n            }\n\n            Event::SetYear { year } => {\n                let year = *year;\n                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx| {\n                    ctx.visible_year = year;\n                }).with_effect(announce_month_effect()))\n            }\n\n            // ── Keyboard navigation ──────────────────────────────────────\n            Event::KeyDown { key, shift } => handle_keydown(*key, *shift, ctx),\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn connect<'a>(\n        state: &'a Self::State,\n        ctx: &'a Self::Context,\n        props: &'a Self::Props,\n        send: &'a dyn Fn(Event),\n    ) -> Self::Api<'a> {\n        Api::new(state, ctx, props, send)\n    }\n}\n\nfn step_for_page_behavior(ctx: &Context) -> i32 {\n    match ctx.page_behavior {\n        PageBehavior::Visible => i32::try_from(ctx.visible_months).unwrap_or(1).max(1),\n        PageBehavior::Single  => 1,\n    }\n}\n\nfn month_step_plan(step: i32) -> TransitionPlan<Machine> {\n    TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx: &mut Context| { ctx.advance_month(step); }\n    if ctx.is_date_disabled(&date) || ctx.is_date_unavailable(&date) { return None; }\n    Some(TransitionPlan::to(State::Focused).apply(move |ctx: &mut Context| {\n        ctx.value.set(Some(date.clone()));\n        ctx.focused_date = date;\n    }))\n}\n\nfn apply_toggle_multi(ctx: &Context, date: CalendarDate)\n    -> Option<TransitionPlan<Machine>>\n{\n    if ctx.readonly { return None; }\n    if ctx.is_date_disabled(&date) || ctx.is_date_unavailable(&date) { return None; }\n    let already_selected = ctx.selected_dates.get().contains(&date);\n    let at_cap = !already_selected && ctx.max_selected\n        .is_some_and(|cap| ctx.selected_dates.get().len() >= cap);\n    if at_cap { return None;   "new_string": "    /// Whether the prev button should be disabled (min constraint).\n    pub fn is_prev_disabled(&self) -> bool {\n        let Some(min) = &self.ctx.min else { return false; };\n        let Ok(first_of_visible) =\n            CalendarDate::new_gregorian(self.ctx.visible_year, self.ctx.visible_month, 1)\n        else { return false; };\n        !matches!(first_of_visible.compare(min), Ordering::Greater)\n    }\n\n    /// Whether the next button should be disabled (max constraint).\n    /// Checks against the **last** visible month so multi-month layouts\n    /// behave correctly.\n    pub fn is_next_disabled(&self) -> bool {\n        let Some(max) = &self.ctx.max else { return false; };\n        let last_offset = self.ctx.visible_months.saturating_sub(1);\n        let (month, year) = self.ctx.month_year_at_offset(last_offset);\n        let Ok(first_of_last) = CalendarDate::new_gregorian(year, month, 1) else {\n            return false;\n        };\n        let days_in_month = first_of_last.days_in_month();\n        let Ok(last_of_last) = CalendarDate::new_gregorian(year, month, days_in_month) else {\n            return false;\n        };\n        !matches!(last_of_last.compare(max), Ordering::Less)\n    }"
}

1440	**Locale-aware week start:**
1441	
1442	| Locale                                               | First Day of Week |
1443	| ---------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- |
1444	| `en-US`, `en-CA`, `ja-JP`, `ko-KR`, `zh-TW`          | Sunday            |
1445	| `ar-SA`, `he-IL`                                     | Sunday            |

1447	| `fa-IR`                                              | Saturday          |
1448	
1449	The `first_day_of_week` prop overrides the locale default when provided.
1450	
1451	### 4.2 First Day of Week
1452	
1453	1. Default derived from locale via ICU4X `WeekCalculator` (US: Sunday, most of Europe: Monday, parts of Middle East: Saturday).
1454	2. Overridable via `first_day_of_week: Option<Weekday>` prop.
1455	3. In RTL locales, the calendar grid is mirrored horizontally (week starts from the right).
1456	4. DateField weekday segment typeahead matches locale-appropriate day names.
1457	
1458	### 4.3 Week Numbers
1459	
1460	1. Optional `show_week_numbers: bool` prop (default `false`).
1461	2. Week numbering follows locale convention: ISO 8601 (most of world) vs US week numbering via ICU4X `WeekCalculator`.
1462	3. Week number column header has `aria-label="Week number"` (localized).
1463	4. Each week number cell has `aria-label="Week {n}"` (localized).
1464	5. Week numbers are not focusable or selectable by default.

1510	When `max_selected` is set, the `ToggleDate` transition guards against `selected_dates.len() >= max_selected`. Excess selections are silently prevented.
1511	
1512	### 5.5 Keyboard
1513	
1514	| Key           | Behavior                                  |
1515	| ------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
1516	| Space / Enter | Toggle focused date in/out of selection   |
1517	| Shift+Space   | Select range from anchor to focused       |
1518	| Ctrl+A        | Select all visible dates in current month |
1519	
1520	## 6. Library Parity
1521	
1522	> Compared against: React Aria (`Calendar`).
1523	
1524	### 6.1 Props
1525	
1526	| Feature                    | ars-ui                                | React Aria                    | Notes                                                             |
1527	| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
1528	| Controlled value           | `value: Option<Option<CalendarDate>>` | `value: DateValue`            | Equivalent                                                        |
1529	| Default value              | `default_value`                       | `defaultValue`                | Equivalent                                                        |
1530	| Focused value (controlled) | --                                    | `focusedValue`                | ars-ui has `focused_date` in Context but not as a controlled prop |
1531	| Default focused value      | --                                    | `defaultFocusedValue`         | ars-ui derives from value/today                                   |
1532	| Min/max                    | `min`, `max`                          | `minValue`, `maxValue`        | Equivalent                                                        |
1533	| Unavailable predicate      | `is_date_unavailable`                 | `isDateUnavailable`           | Equivalent                                                        |
1534	| Disabled                   | `disabled`                            | `isDisabled`                  | Equivalent                                                        |
1535	| Read-only                  | `readonly`                            | `isReadOnly`                  | Equivalent                                                        |

Excess selections are silently prevented.\n\n### 5.5 Keyboard\n\n| Key           | Behavior                                  |\n| ------------- | ----------------------------------------- |\n| Space / Enter | Toggle focused date in/out of selection   |\n| Shift+Space   | Select range from anchor to focused       |\n| Ctrl+A        | Select all visible dates in current month |",
  "new_string": "## 5. Variant: Multiple Selection\n\nCalendar supports multiple non-contiguous date selection alongside the\ndefault single-date mode. The Props, Context, and Event surface for\nmulti-select live directly in §1.2-§1.4 (not as \"additional\"\ndeclarations) — the machine is one unified type that switches behaviour\non `selection_mode` rather than two parallel `Machine` types.\n\n### 5.1 Active surface\n\nThe unified surface relevant to multi-select:\n\n- [`SelectionMode { Single, Multiple }`](#14-props) on `Props` and\n  `Context`.\n- `Props.selected_dates: Option<SelectedDates>` (controlled) and\n  `Props.default_selected_dates: SelectedDates` (uncontrolled), backing\n  `Context.selected_dates: Bindable<SelectedDates>`.\n- `Props.max_selected: Option<usize>` and `Context.max_selected`.\n- [`Event::ToggleDate { date }`](#12-events) struct variant. `SelectDate`\n  is accepted in `Multiple` mode and routes to the same toggle handler so\n  adapters that do not know the active mode can emit one canonical\n  \"select this date\" event.\n\n### 5.2 Behavior\n\n| Action     | Click                 |\n| ---------- | --------------------- |\n| `Multiple` | Toggle date selection |\n\nWhen `max_selected` is set, the `ToggleDate` transition guards against\n`selected_dates.len() >= max_selected`. Toggles that would add a date\nbeyond the cap are silently dropped; toggles that remove an already-selected\ndate always succeed.\n\n### 5.3 Keyboard\n\n| Key             | Behavior                                |\n| --------------- | --------------------------------------- |\n| `Space` / `Enter` | Toggle focused date in/out of selection |\n\nAdvanced multi-select keyboard operations (`Shift+Click`,\n`Shift+Space` range fill from an anchor, `Ctrl+A` select-all visible)\nare not part of this implementation. They require an \"anchor\" concept\nnot currently in the spec or machine state, and are tracked as a\nfollow-up that will refine §5 once a concrete anchor design lands."

1	//! Shared callback wrapper for event handler closures.
2	//!
3	//! [`Callback`] wraps closures in [`Arc`](alloc::sync::Arc) so they can be
4	//! stored in Props structs, cloned cheaply, and
5	//! compared by pointer identity. `Clone`, `PartialEq`, `Deref`, and `AsRef`
6	//! all delegate to `Arc` with no cfg-gated code.
7	//!
8	//! ## Thread-safety
9	//!
10	//! All public constructors (`new`, `new_void`, `From`, [`callback`]) require
11	//! `Send + Sync` bounds on the wrapped closure, and the trait objects in the
12	//! type signatures (`dyn Fn(...) + Send + Sync`) carry those bounds so
13	//! `Callback<…>` is itself `Send + Sync`. This is necessary for adapter
14	//! crates whose framework requires cleanup/effect closures to be
15	//! thread-safe (e.g. Leptos's `on_cleanup`).
16	
17	use alloc::sync::Arc;
18	use core::{
19	    fmt::{self, Debug},
20	    ops::Deref,
21	};
22	
23	/// Shared callback wrapper for event handler closures in Props structs.
24	///
25	/// Wraps closures in [`Arc`] (`Arc`) on every target. This is distinct from
26	/// [`MessageFn`](crate::MessageFn) (used for i18n message closures) and
27	/// [`CleanupFn`](crate::CleanupFn) (used for effect cleanup).
28	///
29	/// Supports an optional return type via
30	/// `Callback<dyn Fn(Args) -> Out + Send + Sync>`. When the return type is
31	/// `()`, write `Callback<dyn Fn(Args) + Send + Sync>` as shorthand.
32	///
33	/// The trait object always carries `+ Send + Sync` so `Callback<T>` is
34	/// itself `Send + Sync`. All public constructors enforce that bound on the
35	/// closure being wrapped.
36	pub struct Callback<T: ?Sized>(pub(crate) Arc<T>);
37	
38	impl<T: ?Sized> Clone for Callback<T> {
39	    fn clone(&self) -> Self {
40	        Callback(Arc::clone(&self.0))
41	    }
42	}
43	
44	impl<T: ?Sized> Debug for Callback<T> {
45	    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
46	        f.write_str("Callback(..)")
47	    }
48	}
49	
50	impl<T: ?Sized> PartialEq for Callback<T> {
51	    fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
52	        Arc::ptr_eq(&self.0, &other.0)
53	    }
54	}
55	
56	impl<T: ?Sized> Deref for Callback<T> {
57	    type Target = T;
58	
59	    fn deref(&self) -> &T {
60	        &self.0
61	    }
62	}
63	
64	impl<T: ?Sized> AsRef<T> for Callback<T> {
65	    fn as_ref(&self) -> &T {
66	        self.0.as_ref()
67	    }
68	}
69	
70	// ── Constructors for Callback<dyn Fn(Args) -> Out + Send + Sync> ───
71	// These use raw Arc construction for dyn trait object coercion.
72	
73	/// Constructor for `Callback<dyn Fn(Args) -> Out + Send + Sync>`.
74	impl<Args: 'static, Out: 'static> Callback<dyn Fn(Args) -> Out + Send + Sync> {
75	    /// Creates a new callback wrapping the given closure.
76	    pub fn new(f: impl Fn(Args) -> Out + Send + Sync + 'static) -> Self {
77	        Self(Arc::new(f))
78	    }
79	}
80	
81	impl<F: Fn(Args) -> Out + Send + Sync + 'static, Args: 'static, Out: 'static> From<F>
82	    for Callback<dyn Fn(Args) -> Out + Send + Sync>
83	{
84	    fn from(f: F) -> Self {
85	        Callback(Arc::new(f))
86	    }
87	}
88	
89	// ── Constructors for Callback<dyn Fn() + Send + Sync> (zero-argument) ─
90	// `dyn Fn() + Send + Sync` and `dyn Fn(Args) -> Out + Send + Sync` are
91	// distinct trait objects in Rust, so the generic `Callback::new` cannot
92	// produce `Callback<dyn Fn() + Send + Sync>`.
93	
94	/// Constructor for zero-argument `Callback<dyn Fn() + Send + Sync>`.
95	impl Callback<dyn Fn() + Send + Sync> {
96	    /// Creates a new zero-argument callback wrapping the given closure.
97	    pub fn new_void(f: impl Fn() + Send + Sync + 'static) -> Self {
98	        Self(Arc::new(f))
99	    }
100	}
101	
102	impl<F: Fn() + Send + Sync + 'static> From<F> for Callback<dyn Fn() + Send + Sync> {
103	    fn from(f: F) -> Self {
104	        Callback(Arc::new(f))
105	    }
106	}
107	
108	// ── Free function constructor ──────────────────────────────────────
109	
110	/// Ergonomic constructor for [`Callback`] with better type inference.
111	///
112	/// The compiler can infer `Args` from the closure signature without
113	/// requiring turbofish syntax.
114	pub fn callback<Args: 'static, Out: 'static>(
115	    f: impl Fn(Args) -> Out + Send + Sync + 'static,
116	) -> Callback<dyn Fn(Args) -> Out + Send + Sync> {
117	    Callback::new(f)
118	}

> AGENT

Reverted, 118 tests still pass.

**Yes, there is one blocking reason:** `Callback::new` (and the `From` impl) at [crates/ars-core/src/callback.rs:74](crates/ars-core/src/callback.rs:74) require `Args: 'static`:

```rust
impl<Args: 'static, Out: 'static> Callback<dyn Fn(Args) -> Out + Send + Sync> {
    pub fn new(f: impl Fn(Args) -> Out + Send + Sync + 'static) -> Self { ... }
}
```

For our predicate, `Args` would need to be `&CalendarDate`, which is not `'static`. The trait object slot is actually `dyn for<'a> Fn(&'a CalendarDate) -> bool + Send + Sync` (HRTB elision), and there's no constructor in `Callback`'s public surface that accepts a higher-ranked closure over a reference argument — the `Arc` field is `pub(crate)`, so we can't fall through to raw `Arc::new` from outside `ars-core` either.

There's no current user of `Callback<dyn Fn(&T) ...>` in the workspace, so it's an unproven path. Two ways to enable it:

1. **Extend `Callback` in ars-core** with a sibling constructor:
   ```rust
   impl<T: ?Sized + 'static, Out: 'static> Callback<dyn for<'a> Fn(&'a T) -> Out + Send + Sync> {
       pub fn new_ref(f: impl for<'a> Fn(&'a T) -> Out + Send + Sync + 'static) -> Self {
           Self(Arc::new(f))
       }
   }
   ```
   Small, additive change. After that, `Calendar` (and any future component with predicate Props) can drop the manual `PartialEq` + accept closures with captured state.

2. **Keep `fn` pointer** — the trade-off I already wrote up in the spec/code.

Want me to do (1) in this same PR (the change is ~10 lines in `ars-core`)? It's a workspace-wide ergonomics win and `Calendar`'s predicate would be the proof case. Or keep (2) and file it as a follow-up.

This sibling\n// constructor accepts a higher-ranked closure over a reference argument\n// so predicate-style Props fields (e.g. `Calendar::is_date_unavailable`)\n// can still use `Callback` without falling back to raw `fn` pointers.\n\n/// Constructor for `Callback<dyn for<'a> Fn(&'a T) -> Out + Send + Sync>`.\nimpl<T: ?Sized + 'static, Out: 'static> Callback<dyn for<'a> Fn(&'a T) -> Out + Send + Sync> {\n    /// Creates a new callback wrapping a higher-ranked closure over a\n    /// reference argument.\n    ///\n    /// Use when the closure signature is `Fn(&T) -> Out` (predicates,\n    /// transformers, key extractors) — the regular [`Callback::new`]\n    /// constructor cannot satisfy the implicit HRTB lifetime because its\n    /// `Args: 'static` bound excludes reference types.\n    pub fn new_ref(f: impl for<'a> Fn(&'a T) -> Out + Send + Sync + 'static) -> Self {\n        Self(Arc::new(f))\n    }\n}\n\n// ── Constructors for Callback<dyn Fn() + Send + Sync> (zero-argument) ─\n// `dyn Fn() + Send + Sync` and `dyn Fn(Args) -> Out + Send + Sync` are\n// distinct trait objects in Rust, so the generic `Callback::new` cannot\n// produce `Callback<dyn Fn() + Send + Sync>`."
