263	/// Predicate type for marking dates unavailable.
264	///
265	/// A bare `fn` pointer (not a closure) keeps `Props` `Clone + PartialEq`
266	/// without bespoke comparison logic; applications that need richer

270	
271	/// Props for the Calendar component.
272	///
273	/// `PartialEq` is implemented by hand rather than derived because
274	/// `is_date_unavailable` is a raw function pointer; the auto-derived
275	/// `PartialEq` would compare those pointers directly and surface a
276	/// `unpredictable_function_pointer_comparisons` lint. The manual impl uses
277	/// `core::ptr::fn_addr_eq` for predicate equality and field-wise equality
278	/// everywhere else.
279	#[derive(Clone, Debug, HasId)]
280	pub struct Props {
281	    /// Component instance ID.
282	    pub id: String,
283	    /// Controlled single-date value.
284	    pub value: Option<Option<CalendarDate>>,
285	    /// Default date for uncontrolled single-select mode.
286	    pub default_value: Option<CalendarDate>,
287	    /// Controlled multi-selection set.
288	    pub selected_dates: Option<SelectedDates>,
289	    /// Default selection set for uncontrolled multi-select mode.
290	    pub default_selected_dates: SelectedDates,
291	    /// Selection mode — single by default. Multi-select unlocks
292	    /// `selected_dates` and the `ToggleDate` event.
293	    pub selection_mode: SelectionMode,
294	    /// Maximum number of dates that can be selected in `Multiple` mode.
295	    /// `None` removes the cap; excess toggles are silently dropped.
296	    pub max_selected: Option<usize>,
297	    /// Minimum selectable date.
298	    pub min: Option<CalendarDate>,
299	    /// Maximum selectable date.
300	    pub max: Option<CalendarDate>,
301	    /// Whether the entire calendar is non-interactive.
302	    pub disabled: bool,
303	    /// Whether the calendar allows navigation but not selection.
304	    pub readonly: bool,
305	    /// Predicate returning true for dates that should be marked unavailable.
306	    /// Unavailable dates are focusable but not selectable.
307	    pub is_date_unavailable: Option<IsDateUnavailableFn>,
308	    /// Explicit override of the locale's default first day of week.
309	    /// When `Some`, overrides the locale default. When `None`, derives from
310	    /// `ars_i18n::Locale` via `WeekInfo::first_day`.
311	    ///
312	    /// **CLDR Limitations**: The CLDR `WeekInfo::first_day` data covers most locales but
313	    /// may not account for religious or cultural contexts where the first day differs from
314	    /// the national default (e.g., Islamic calendars where Friday is the start of the week
315	    /// in religious contexts, even though Saturday is the CLDR default for `ar-SA`).
316	    /// Applications serving these contexts SHOULD use `first_day_of_week: Some(Weekday::Friday)`
317	    /// explicitly rather than relying on CLDR locale data.
318	    pub first_day_of_week: Option<Weekday>,
319	    /// Whether to display ISO week numbers at the start of each calendar row.
320	    pub show_week_numbers: bool,
321	    /// Right-to-left layout direction.
322	    pub is_rtl: bool,
323	    /// Number of months to display side-by-side. Values below 1 are
324	    /// clamped to 1 by `Machine::init`. Default: 1.
325	    pub visible_months: usize,
326	    /// Controls navigation step size. Default: `PageBehavior::Visible`.
327	    pub page_behavior: PageBehavior,
328	    /// The "today" date, injected by the adapter for testability.
329	    pub today: CalendarDate,
330	}

332	impl PartialEq for Props {
333	    fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
334	        let predicates_eq = match (self.is_date_unavailable, other.is_date_unavailable) {
335	            (None, None) => true,
336	            (Some(a), Some(b)) => core::ptr::fn_addr_eq(a, b),

Two new `ars-core` unit tests cover `Callback::new_ref`.\n\n- Coverage on the new module sits at ≥95% line and ≥95% branch for both\n  `calendar/mod.rs` and `calendar/grid.rs`. Multi-month layouts use this so triggers in later grids do\n    /// not get flagged `data-ars-outside-month` just because they belong\n    /// to a different month than offset 0.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn cell_trigger_attrs_for(&self, date: &CalendarDate, offset: usize) -> AttrMap {\n        self.cell_trigger_attrs_inner(date, Some(offset))\n    }\n\n    fn cell_trigger_attrs_inner(&self, date: &CalendarDate, offset: Option<usize>) -> AttrMap {\n        let mut attrs = AttrMap::new();\n        let [(scope_attr, scope_val), (part_attr, part_val)] =\n            Part::CellTrigger { date: date.clone() }.data_attrs();\n\n        attrs.set(scope_attr, scope_val).set(part_attr, part_val);\n\n        let disabled = self.is_disabled(date);\n        let unavailable = self.is_unavailable(date);\n        let is_focused = &self.ctx.focused_date == date;\n        let is_today = self.is_today(date);\n        let selected = self.is_selected(date);\n\n        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::TabIndex, if is_focused { \"0\" } else { \"-1\" });\n\n        // `aria-disabled` announces the semantic restriction for both\n        // out-of-range (disabled) and unavailable dates.   "old_string": "fn month_step_plan(step: i32) -> TransitionPlan<Machine> {\n    TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx: &mut Context| { ctx.advance_month(step); })\n        .with_effect(announce_month_effect())\n}",
  "new_string": "fn month_step_plan(step: i32) -> TransitionPlan<Machine> {\n    TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx: &mut Context| {\n        ctx.advance_month(step);\n        // Keep `focused_date` aligned with the newly visible range so the\n        // roving-tabindex target still has a rendered cell. Without this,\n        // paging from Jan 15 → Feb leaves focused_date on Jan 15, which is\n        // not in February's 6-week grid, and no cell gets `tabindex=\"0\"`.\n        // The shifted date is clamped into the configured `[min, max]`\n        // range so out-of-range targets snap back to the boundary.\n        if let Ok(shifted) = ctx.focused_date.add(DateDuration {\n            months: step,\n            ..DateDuration::default()\n        }) {\n            ctx.focused_date = ctx.clamp_date(shifted);\n        }\n    })\n    .with_effect(announce_month_effect())\n}"
}

Multi-month layouts use this so triggers in later grids do\n    /// not get flagged `data-ars-outside-month` just because they belong\n    /// to a different month than offset 0.\n    pub fn cell_trigger_attrs_for(&self, date: &CalendarDate, offset: usize) -> AttrMap {\n        self.cell_trigger_attrs_inner(date, Some(offset))\n    }\n\n    fn cell_trigger_attrs_inner(&self, date: &CalendarDate, offset: Option<usize>) -> AttrMap {\n        let mut attrs = AttrMap::new();\n        let [(scope_attr, scope_val), (part_attr, part_val)] = Part::CellTrigger { date: date.clone() }.data_attrs();\n        attrs.set(scope_attr, scope_val);\n        attrs.set(part_attr, part_val);\n\n        let disabled = self.is_disabled(date);\n        let unavailable = self.is_unavailable(date);\n        let is_focused = self.ctx.focused_date == *date;\n        let is_today = *date == self.ctx.today;\n        let selected = self.is_selected(date);\n\n        // tabindex: only the focused cell or the first selectable cell is tabbable.\n        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::TabIndex, if is_focused { \"0\" } else { \"-1\" });\n\n        // `aria-disabled` announces the semantic restriction for both\n        // out-of-range (disabled) and unavailable dates. HTML `disabled`\n        // is **only** set for the disabled case because it removes the\n        // element from the browser focus model; unavailable dates must\n        // remain focusable per spec §3 even though they cannot be selected.\n        if disabled || unavailable {\n            attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Disabled), \"true\");\n        }\n        if disabled {\n            attrs.set_bool(HtmlAttr::Disabled, true);\n        }\n        if selected {\n            attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Selected), \"true\");\n        }\n        if is_today {\n            attrs.set_bool(HtmlAttr::Data(\"ars-today\"), true);\n        }\n        let outside_month = match offset {\n            Some(o) => self.ctx.is_outside_month_at_offset(date, o),\n            None    => self.ctx.is_outside_visible_month(date),\n        };\n        if outside_month {\n            attrs.set_bool(HtmlAttr::Data(\"ars-outside-month\"), true);\n        }\n        if unavailable {\n            attrs.set_bool(HtmlAttr::Data(\"ars-unavailable\"), true);\n        }\n\n        // aria-label: full date string for screen readers.\n        // Unavailable and disabled dates append a suffix so screen readers announce\n        // the restriction without requiring the user to attempt selection.\n        let base_label = format!(\n            \"{} {}, {}, {}\",\n            self.ctx.intl_backend.month_long_name(date.month(), &self.ctx.locale),\n            date.day(),\n            date.year(),\n            self.ctx.intl_backend.weekday_long_label(date.weekday(), &self.ctx.locale),\n        );\n        let label = if unavailable {\n            format!(\"{} (unavailable)\", base_label)\n        } else if disabled {\n            format!(\"{} (disabled)\", base_label)\n        } else {\n            base_label\n        };\n        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Label), label);\n\n        attrs\n    }"
}

  "old_string": "fn month_step_plan(step: i32) -> TransitionPlan<Machine> {\n    TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx: &mut Context| {\n        ctx.advance_month(step);\n        // Keep `focused_date` aligned with the newly visible range so the\n        // roving-tabindex target still has a rendered cell. Without this,\n        // paging from Jan 15 → Feb leaves focused_date on Jan 15, which is\n        // not in February's 6-week grid, and no cell gets `tabindex=\"0\"`.\n        // The shifted date is clamped into the configured `[min, max]`\n        // range so out-of-range targets snap back to the boundary.\n        if let Ok(shifted) = ctx.focused_date.add(ars_i18n::DateDuration {\n            months: step,\n            ..ars_i18n::DateDuration::default()\n        }) {\n            ctx.focused_date = ctx.clamp_date(shifted);\n        }\n    })\n    .with_effect(announce_month_effect())\n}",
  "new_string": "fn month_step_plan(step: i32) -> TransitionPlan<Machine> {\n    TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx: &mut Context| {\n        // `visible_month/year` and `focused_date` must advance atomically.\n        // If the focused-date shift fails near a representable calendar\n        // boundary, leave both untouched so the roving-tabindex target\n        // can never end up outside the rendered grid. The clamp keeps\n        // out-of-range targets snapped to `[min, max]`.\n        let Ok(shifted) = ctx.focused_date.add(ars_i18n::DateDuration {\n            months: step,\n            ..ars_i18n::DateDuration::default()\n        }) else {\n            return;\n        };\n        ctx.advance_month(step);\n        ctx.focused_date = ctx.clamp_date(shifted);\n    })\n    .with_effect(announce_month_effect())\n}"
}

  "old_string": "fn month_step_plan(step: i32) -> TransitionPlan<Machine> {\n    TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx: &mut Context| {\n        ctx.advance_month(step);\n        // Keep `focused_date` aligned with the newly visible range so the\n        // roving-tabindex target still has a rendered cell. Without this,\n        // paging from Jan 15 → Feb leaves focused_date on Jan 15, which is\n        // not in February's 6-week grid, and no cell gets `tabindex=\"0\"`.\n        // The shifted date is clamped into the configured `[min, max]`\n        // range so out-of-range targets snap back to the boundary.\n        if let Ok(shifted) = ctx.focused_date.add(DateDuration {\n            months: step,\n            ..DateDuration::default()\n        }) {\n            ctx.focused_date = ctx.clamp_date(shifted);\n        }\n    })\n    .with_effect(announce_month_effect())\n}",
  "new_string": "fn month_step_plan(step: i32) -> TransitionPlan<Machine> {\n    TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx: &mut Context| {\n        // `visible_month/year` and `focused_date` must advance atomically.\n        // If the focused-date shift fails near a representable calendar\n        // boundary, leave both untouched so the roving-tabindex target\n        // can never end up outside the rendered grid. The clamp keeps\n        // out-of-range targets snapped to `[min, max]`.\n        let Ok(shifted) = ctx.focused_date.add(DateDuration {\n            months: step,\n            ..DateDuration::default()\n        }) else {\n            return;\n        };\n        ctx.advance_month(step);\n        ctx.focused_date = ctx.clamp_date(shifted);\n    })\n    .with_effect(announce_month_effect())\n}\n\nfn sync_props_into_ctx(ctx: &mut Context, props: &Props) {\n    ctx.value.sync_controlled(props.value.clone());\n    ctx.selected_dates.sync_controlled(props.selected_dates.clone());\n\n    ctx.selection_mode = props.selection_mode;\n    ctx.max_selected = props.max_selected;\n    ctx.min = props.min.clone();\n    ctx.max = props.max.clone();\n    ctx.disabled = props.disabled;\n    ctx.readonly = props.readonly;\n    ctx.is_date_unavailable_fn = props.is_date_unavailable.clone();\n    ctx.show_week_numbers = props.show_week_numbers;\n    ctx.is_rtl = props.is_rtl;\n    ctx.visible_months = props.visible_months.max(1);\n    ctx.page_behavior = props.page_behavior;\n    ctx.today = props.today.clone();\n\n    if let Some(fdow) = props.first_day_of_week {\n        ctx.first_day_of_week = fdow;\n    }\n\n    // Re-clamp `focused_date` in case `min`/`max` tightened.\n    let clamped = ctx.clamp_date(ctx.focused_date.clone());\n    ctx.focused_date = clamped;\n}"
}

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6E3GQ1 (crates/ars-components/src/date_time/calendar/mod.rs:967) ===
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Add prop-sync transitions for calendar context fields**

This machine snapshots controlled and context-backed props only in `init`, but it never implements `Machine::on_props_changed`, so `Service::set_props` cannot enqueue any sync event. As a result, runtime prop updates are ignored: controlled `value`/`selected_dates` never receive `sync_controlled`, and context-backed flags like `disabled`, `readonly`, `min`, and `max` stay stale after parent updates. In controlled adapter usage, this causes the calendar to diverge from parent state until remount.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6E3GQ5 (crates/ars-components/src/date_time/calendar/mod.rs:1129) ===
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve a visible roving focus target on SetMonth**

`SetMonth` updates only `visible_month` and leaves `focused_date` untouched, unlike `month_step_plan` which explicitly realigns focus. Jumping months via this event can leave `focused_date` outside the rendered 6-week grid (e.g., January focus then jump to July), so no cell gets `tabindex="0"` and keyboard roving focus loses its anchor.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6E3GQ7 (crates/ars-components/src/date_time/calendar/mod.rs:1901) ===
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Compute prev disabled state from actual page step**

The previous-button guard ignores `page_behavior` and disables as soon as the current first visible month is at/before `min`, which is too strict when `visible_months > 1` and paging is `Single`. In that mode, moving back by one month can still leave selectable dates in view (e.g., Mar–May with `min=2024-03-15` should still allow navigating to Feb–Apr), but this check disables navigation early.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6E3GQ- (crates/ars-components/src/date_time/calendar/mod.rs:1932) ===
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Compute next disabled state from actual page step**

The next-button guard always compares `max` against the last day of the currently rendered last month, regardless of whether paging advances by one month or by the full visible range. With multi-month + `PageBehavior::Single`, this disables too early: the next page may still include selectable dates within `max` even though the current trailing month extends past `max`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6E3GRF (crates/ars-components/src/date_time/calendar/mod.rs:1481) ===
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Mark nav triggers disabled when calendar is disabled**

When `ctx.disabled` is true, the machine blocks navigation events, but `prev_trigger_attrs`/`next_trigger_attrs` only set `disabled`/`aria-disabled` when min/max boundaries are hit. This leaves navigation buttons exposed as enabled controls that do nothing, creating inconsistent disabled semantics and misleading assistive-tech output for a globally disabled calendar.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6E3GRI (crates/ars-components/src/date_time/calendar/mod.rs:1146) ===
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve a visible roving focus target on SetYear**

`SetYear` updates only `visible_year` and leaves `focused_date` unchanged, so jumping years can strand roving focus on a date that is no longer rendered in the new year view. In that state, no rendered cell matches `focused_date`, so every cell gets `tabindex="-1"` and keyboard grid navigation loses its active focus anchor.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

  "new_string": "    /// is globally disabled or stepping back by `page_behavior`'s step\n    /// would yield a visible range with no selectable dates ≥ `min`.\n    ///\n    /// The check honours [`PageBehavior::Single`] vs [`PageBehavior::Visible`]:\n    /// with multi-month + `Single`, paging back by one month may still\n    /// produce a range that contains selectable dates even if the current\n    /// first visible month already starts at-or-before `min`.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn is_prev_disabled(&self) -> bool {\n        if self.ctx.disabled {\n            return true;\n        }\n\n        let Some(min) = &self.ctx.min else {\n            return false;\n        };\n\n        // Compute the LAST visible month after pressing prev. If even its\n        // last day is below `min`, the next page back has no selectable\n        // dates and prev is disabled.\n        let step = self.nav_step_size();\n        let (new_first_month, new_first_year) = advance_month_pair(\n            self.ctx.visible_month,\n            self.ctx.visible_year,\n            -i32::try_from(step).unwrap_or(1),\n        );\n        let last_offset = self.ctx.visible_months.saturating_sub(1);\n        let (new_last_month, new_last_year) =\n            grid_month_year_at_offset(new_first_month, new_first_year, last_offset);\n\n        let Ok(first_of_new_last) =\n            CalendarDate::new_gregorian(new_last_year, new_last_month, 1)\n        else {\n            return false;\n        };\n        let days_in_month = first_of_new_last.days_in_month();\n        let Ok(last_of_new_last) =\n            CalendarDate::new_gregorian(new_last_year, new_last_month, days_in_month)\n        else {\n            return false;\n        };\n\n        matches!(last_of_new_last.compare(min), Ordering::Less)\n    }\n\n    /// Whether the next-trigger should be disabled — either the calendar\n    /// is globally disabled or stepping forward by `page_behavior`'s step\n    /// would yield a visible range with no selectable dates ≤ `max`.\n    ///\n    /// Symmetric to [`Api::is_prev_disabled`]: the check honours\n    /// [`PageBehavior::Single`] vs [`PageBehavior::Visible`] so multi-month\n    /// + single-step paging doesn't disable too early.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn is_next_disabled(&self) -> bool {\n        if self.ctx.disabled {\n            return true;\n        }\n\n        let Some(max) = &self.ctx.max else {\n            return false;\n        };\n\n        // Compute the FIRST visible month after pressing next. If its\n        // first day is already above `max`, the next page forward has no\n        // selectable dates and next is disabled.\n        let step = self.nav_step_size();\n        let (new_first_month, new_first_year) = advance_month_pair(\n            self.ctx.visible_month,\n            self.ctx.visible_year,\n            i32::try_from(step).unwrap_or(1),\n        );\n        let Ok(first_of_new_first) =\n            CalendarDate::new_gregorian(new_first_year, new_first_month, 1)\n        else {\n            return false;\n        };\n\n        matches!(first_of_new_first.compare(max), Ordering::Greater)\n    }"
